nodes.label: Tendril Network Hub Metaphor
nodes.rationale: The hero art depicts a single central figure grasping many bundles of threads that radiate outward to the edges of the frame, over a backdrop of branching lightning/tendril textures. This visually encodes the Tendril product idea: a central coordinator holding many outbound connections (nodes/leases/tunnels), i.e. one hub managing many distributed endpoints. The classical engraving style rendered in electric blue suggests old-world craft fused with electric/technical infrastructure.

nodes.label: Tendril Open Graph Social Preview
nodes.rationale: Dark full-bleed canvas with centered serif wordmark and muted tagline; built as a link-unfurl card, not in-app UI.

nodes.label: The last mile of funding
nodes.rationale: Tagline positions Tendril as completing the final step of funding rather than originating it; muted gray under the wordmark subordinates positioning to brand.

nodes.label: Ephemeral Docker Container Sandbox
nodes.rationale: Trust boundary is not a permissions system but an ephemeral container: no host mounts, no inbound ports (bore dials out), capabilities dropped, cgroup caps, destroyed when the paid lease ends. Same containerization trade-off the DePIN compute sector runs on, made prepaid and individual-scale.

nodes.label: Payment as Identity
nodes.rationale: Payment is the identity: a brand-new address can pay on its very first request with no sign-up or sign-in. Credit is keyed to the sender of the settled transaction, never to anything the client claims about itself.

nodes.label: Verify-Then-Settle Ordering
nodes.rationale: Settlement ordering is verify, do the work, then settle: the facilitator verifies the payment group by simulation, the backend provisions, and only then is payment settled on-chain, so a sandbox that fails to start (503) costs the caller nothing.

nodes.label: Custodial Model
nodes.rationale: Payments pool at one platform address and credit is an off-chain ledger in Neon with one schema per network; every payment is recorded by txid so replaying one cannot credit twice.

nodes.label: Per-Network Ledger Isolation
nodes.rationale: The two ledgers never mix: one database, one Postgres schema per network (testnet.* / mainnet.*), search_path resolves every query to that network's tables, so testnet play money can never be read as a mainnet balance.

nodes.label: CORS-Free Payable Routes
nodes.rationale: Payable routes answer any origin so a browser anywhere can pay one; the Tendril web app has no privileged access and the frontend is just another x402 client. CORS only ever constrained browsers; a headless agent was never subject to it.

nodes.label: MCP Spend Cap (TENDRIL_MAX_ATOMIC)
nodes.rationale: Before paying, the MCP probes the 402 and reads accepts[0].amount; if it exceeds TENDRIL_MAX_ATOMIC it aborts and nothing settles. Withdraw is intentionally not capped this way: it sends existing earnings all-or-nothing.
